An employer shall submit to STC such information or evidence relating to employees of the employer as STC requires.

Where an employer fails to comply with subsection (1) in relation to an employee, STC may defer payment of a benefit to, or in relation to, an employee where the information sought is relevant to the right to receive the benefit.

heading.b: Employee or claimant to provide information

block.txt: STC may require an employee or a claimant for payment of a benefit under this Act—
to provide STC with specified information or evidence referred to in subsection (2),
to provide STC with an authority to obtain from a third person any such information or evidence, or
in the case of a claimant for a benefit arising in relation to permanent physical or mental incapacity—to undergo a medical examination.

A requirement under subsection (1) may be made only in relation to information, evidence or a medical examination that is relevant to the assessment of an application made by the claimant for payment of the benefit.
Where—

the employee or claimant to whom a requirement under subsection (1) relates fails to comply with the requirement or, in purported compliance with the requirement, makes or provides an untrue statement, or

a person referred to in subsection (1) (b) fails to provide information or evidence that STC has been authorised to obtain from the person or, in purported compliance with the request by STC for the information or evidence, makes or provides an untrue statement,

STC may take such action in relation to the benefit concerned as, in the opinion of STC, would place the claimant as nearly as possible in the same position as the claimant would be if the information or evidence had been provided or the medical examination made or if the statement had not been untrue.
For the purposes of this section, untrue, in relation to a statement, includes—
misleading in the form and context in which the statement appears, and
misleading by reason of the omission from the statement of matter that is material.
A purported assignment of, or purported charge over, a benefit is void.
Where, but for this subsection, a benefit would pass by operation of law to a person other than a person to whom the benefit is payable under this Act, the benefit does not so pass.
A benefit payable on the death of an employee is not an asset in the employee’s estate that is applicable in payment of the debts and liabilities of the deceased.
Nothing in this section prevents STC from making, at the request of a person to whom an amount by way of a benefit is payable, a payment of the whole or a part of the amount on behalf of the person.
Any payment made under subsection (4) shall be deemed to have been made to the person entitled to the benefit.

heading.b: Payment without grant of probate etc

block.txt: Where an employee or former employee or a non-employee spouse dies and—
a benefit or family law superannuation payment is or becomes payable under this Act in relation to the deceased,
production to STC of probate of the will, or letters of administration of the estate, of the deceased has not been arranged, and

STC has not, within the period of 3 months that next succeeds the death of the deceased, received a notice of intention to apply for a grant of probate of the will, or letters of administration of the estate, of the deceased,

STC may, if it so decides, make a payment of the whole or any part of the benefit or family law superannuation payment in accordance with subsection (2), being a payment that does not exceed $50,000 or, where some other amount is prescribed for the purposes of this section, that other amount.
Where STC makes a decision under subsection (1), STC may—
pay the whole or any part of the amount of the benefit or family law superannuation payment to an eligible person within the meaning of Chapter 3 of the Succession Act 2006,
after paying the funeral expenses of the deceased or reimbursing a person who has paid those expenses—pay the whole or any part of the balance to any person referred to in paragraph (a), or
in special circumstances, pay the whole or any part of the amount of the benefit or family law superannuation payment, or the balance referred to in paragraph (b), to some other person.

Where an employee or former employee or a non-employee spouse dies and STC is of the opinion that proceedings might be instituted under Chapter 3 of the Succession Act 2006 in relation to the estate, or notional estate, of the deceased, STC may, despite any other provision of this Act, pay to the personal representatives of the deceased any benefit or family law superannuation payment that, but for this subsection, would have been paid to some other person.

heading.b: Restriction on manner of payment of benefit

block.txt: STC must not pay, in cash or by a cheque which authorises payment in cash on presentation, a benefit or part of a benefit payable under this Act.

heading.b: Recovery of money owing to STC

block.txt: STC may recover any money owing to STC under this Act by an employee, employer or other person, together with interest thereon as provided by subsection (3)—
except in the case of unpaid contributions—as a debt in a court of competent jurisdiction,
where any amount is, or becomes, payable under this Act to the employee, employer or other person—by deduction from that amount, or
in the case of an employee—by deduction from the employee’s salary in accordance with subsection (2) by such instalments and at such times as STC determines.

An employer shall, at the written request of STC, make deductions from an employee’s salary as referred to in subsection (1) (c) and pay the amount thereof to STC, and an amount so deducted and paid shall be deemed to have been paid to STC by the employee from whose salary the deduction was made.

Interest at a rate from time to time determined by STC is payable on any amount owing to STC calculated from the date on which the amount became due for payment until the date on which the amount is recovered under subsection (1) or is otherwise paid.

If STC is unable, after reasonable inquiry, to find a person to whom a benefit is payable, STC may pay the benefit to someone else to be applied wholly for the care, maintenance, benefit and support of any person wholly or partly dependent on the person who would otherwise be entitled to the benefit.
Any payment made under this section is taken to have been made to the person who, but for this section, would be entitled to the benefit.

Where a person to whom a benefit under this Act is payable is, in the opinion of STC, incapable of administering his or her own affairs by reason of illness, imprisonment or any other cause, STC may pay the benefit to some other person to be applied wholly for the care, maintenance, benefit and support of the person to whom, but for this section, the benefit would be payable, or of any person wholly or partly dependent on him or her.
Any payment made under this section shall be deemed to have been made to the person entitled to the benefit.

heading.b: Information that must be disclosed to employees

block.txt: STC must from time to time give to an employee or other person such information as STC determines under this section.

block.txt: This Schedule applies to an employee—
who is of or above the age of 55 years, and
who, as a result of a single reduction of salary, has undergone a reduction of 20% or more in attributed salary after reaching that age, and
whose employer certifies the matters referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b).
The fact that a person undergoes more than one attributed salary reduction of 20% or more does not mean that the person ceases to be a person to whom this Schedule applies.

In this Schedule, exit date, in relation to an employee to whom this Schedule applies, means the day immediately preceding the day of the reduction in attributed salary in relation to which the employee makes an election under clause 3.
An employee to whom this Schedule applies may elect to preserve his or her benefit under this Act in accordance with this Schedule.

An employee may make only one election under this clause but the election may relate to any single reduction in attributed salary of 20% or more that occurs after the employee reaches 55 years of age (not just the first reduction that occurs).
The benefit is preserved from the exit date.

heading.b: Calculation of value of preserved benefit

block.txt: The value of a preserved benefit in respect of an employee to whom this Schedule applies is to be calculated in accordance with section 22 as if the employee had ceased employment.
A benefit preserved under this Schedule may only be paid in accordance with section 24.

heading.b: Calculation of deferred accrued benefit for non-contributing employees

block.txt: (Section 26E)
The deferred accrued benefit provided by Part 4A for an employee is an amount calculated in accordance with whichever of the following provisions is appropriate in the particular case—
FAS= the employee’s final average salary (as defined in section 21), and
Y= the years of eligible service on a daily basis, commencing on or after the appointed day and ending on 30 June 1992.
B= the basic benefit that would have been provided by section 22 if the employee had ceased to be an employee by reason of resignation on 1 July 1992, and

AWOTE factor= the factor calculated as set out below (for the purpose of indexing the benefit (B) in line with movements in average weekly earnings between 30 June 1992 and the final payment/preservation date for the benefit).
The final payment/preservation date for the benefit is the date on which the benefit is payable under section 23 or on which it is required to be preserved under section 24, whichever happens first.

The AWOTE factor is calculated by dividing the AWOTE applicable as at the final payment/preservation date for the benefit by the June 1992 AWOTE. If the AWOTE factor works out to be a number less than 1, it is instead to be taken to be 1.

The AWOTE applicable at the final payment/preservation date for the benefit is the dollar amount last published before that date by the Australian Statistician under the Census and Statistics Act 1905 of the Commonwealth as the amount of average weekly ordinary time earnings.

The June 1992 AWOTE is the dollar amount last published before 30 June 1992 by the Australian Statistician under the Census and Statistics Act 1905 of the Commonwealth as the amount of average weekly ordinary time earnings.
